I've written the screening for advisory 19563 to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/19563.json`; it was a read-only review, nothing was run.
- **Trust decision:** A build-time default token decides whether telemetry is sent (users can opt out with an environment variable). At the pinned commit that default is a hardcoded `"secret"` (`telemetry/config.go:12`), because the release workflows inject `telemetry.auth`, which doesn't match the variable name. An empty token still sends, without the auth header (`telemetry/telemetry.go:145`).
- **`pattern_fit`: B, weak.** The fix never touches the "cluster fingerprint" sent with every event (`telemetry/telemetry.go:320-347`), an unsalted SHA-256 over env vars, raw CLI arguments (including `--secret`) and the whole config file. A solver can dismiss it as "just an anonymous hash".
- **Strongest lever:** the existing branch that sends without a token makes "set the default token to empty" look like a complete fix. The published fix also has to make `NewTracker` disable itself and gate the CLI runner on `Enabled()`.
- **Biggest red flag:** fairness, so no formal flag. The right fix for the fingerprint route is underdetermined, and the published fix adds a new `Enabled()` method that hidden tests could only rely on if the report names it. The fix is also small (about 20 min), and one of its four source files (`metrics/metrics.go`) is an unrelated change.
